meta.challenge: NASA Space Apps: create a health monitoring tool for astronauts
meta.required_app_disclaimer: Educational prototype only. Thresholds are Earth-based adult reference values or study criteria, not NASA flight medical limits. First-aid text is draft guidance, not crew medical orders. The flight surgeon / mission medical team makes the final decision.
meta.data_status: DEMO / RESEARCH CANDIDATE – not clinically validated, not approved for real-world medical use

evidence_levels.A: Checked against the cited NASA/peer-reviewed source during this build.
evidence_levels.B: Team-compiled. A source page or standard is identified, but the exact numbers were not re-verified. Confirm before the final submission.
evidence_levels.C: Team-proposed or Earth-based reference values. Not NASA flight limits. Needs clinical review.

status_types.Numeric: can be color-coded from a number
status_types.Scenario: shown as an information card (no color limits)

important_notes: 1. The columns Recommended_Action and Contact_Ground_When are drafted crew-facing guidance based on the cited sources and general first-aid principles. They need review by a medical professional before any real-world use.
2. Vital-sign limits are Earth-based adult reference values (S18), not NASA flight limits. The tool must show a disclaimer: educational only; the flight surgeon makes the final decision.
3. Rows from the team's earlier sheets (S17) have no recorded original source. Trace each number to its page before submission.
4. Source S05 (CSA 'Why conduct experiments in space') was provided in the resources but has not yet been reviewed.
5. Blood glucose is named in the challenge brief but NASA sources provided here list no glucometer; confirm which devices the app may assume.
audit_notes: CLINICAL SOURCE AUDIT (14 NOV 2026): See Clinical_Evidence_Audit, EtCO2_Review, First_Aid_Audit. These tabs add exact terrestrial clinical references and distinguish research study endpoints from actual alert limits.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION: In the active Status_Checker, RED for fasting glucose >=126 mg/dL is a prototype display, NOT a medical emergency criterion. Likewise EtCO2 >50 mmHg is from a small ED procedural-sedation study, NOT a NASA flight RED limit.
AHA/ACC 2025, ADA 2026, BTS, FDA, NEWS2 and AHA/Red Cross 2024 are EARTH-BASED clinical guidance; the actual spacecraft alert and treatment policy requires mission medical approval.
Existing status formulas were preserved so the demo remains functional. Do NOT treat its colors as validated medical classification or its first-aid text as crew medical orders.

general_first_aid_audit.main_concern_in_original_actions: Generic draft first aid may not be appropriate in microgravity or delayed-communication setting
general_first_aid_audit.evidence_backed_principle: NASA-STD-3001 V1: medical management by Flight Medicine team within mission constraints
general_first_aid_audit.recommended_action_text: Display onboard APPROVED checklists and a clear route to crew medical officer
general_first_aid_audit.do_not_automate: Present unreviewed draft sentences as flight medical orders

legend.meaning: Outside the normal range but not critical
legend.action_focus: Self-care first aid, recheck, log and report
legend.response_time: Recheck in minutes; report the same day if it persists

legend.meaning: Critical value, or a symptom override is present
legend.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon

knowledge_base_severity_to_color.action_focus: Prevention: do the routine measures that stop the problem
knowledge_base_severity_to_color.note: Nothing is wrong now; the guidance is about keeping it that way

knowledge_base_severity_to_color.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists
knowledge_base_severity_to_color.note: Not an emergency; act early so it stays small

knowledge_base_severity_to_color.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day
knowledge_base_severity_to_color.note: Highest YELLOW: do not wait for it to worsen

knowledge_base_severity_to_color.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon
knowledge_base_severity_to_color.note: Follow the emergency procedure; do not delay the call

status_logic.description: Same logic as the Status_Checker sheet. Inputs: metric_id, numeric value, symptom_override (bool). Output: color, state key, guidance.
steps: 1. If value is not a number -> no result. If metric_id unknown -> no result.
2. side = LOW if value < normal_min; HIGH if value > normal_max; else NORMAL.
3. color = RED if symptom_override is true, or (critical_low != null and value < critical_low), or (critical_high != null and value > critical_high).
4. Else color = GREEN if normal_min <= value <= normal_max, otherwise YELLOW.
5. state = GREEN if color is GREEN; RED_SYMPTOM if color is RED and side is NORMAL; else color + "_" + side (e.g. YELLOW_HIGH, RED_LOW).
6. guidance = vital_signs[metric_id].states[state]. If missing (e.g. SpO2 above 100) show "check the value entered".
status_logic.null_critical_limit_means: no numeric RED on that side (EtCO2 critical_low is null on purpose: no validated limit). RED on that side can only come from symptom_override.
status_logic.ui_rule: Show vital_signs[].clinical_evidence_audit.flight_use_decision and the required_app_disclaimer next to any colored result. Do not present colors as validated medical classification.

vital_signs.why_measured_in_space: Microgravity changes circulation and the heart; arrhythmia and infection both show up in heart rate
vital_signs.evidence_note: Original RED low <50 has AHA bradycardia-context support, but RED high >=120 is NOT a universal AHA emergency threshold. Symptoms, ECG, baseline and perfusion matter. DEMO ONLY.

clinical_evidence_audit.grounded_adult_evidence: AHA symptomatic bradyarrhythmia often <50; tachyarrhythmia typically >=150 when appropriate
clinical_evidence_audit.not_established: No validated universal >=120 RED or <50 RED for all astronauts
clinical_evidence_audit.recommendation_for_demo: Resting baseline + repeat measurement, symptoms, ECG/arrhythmia if available. Original cutoffs demo-only.

first_aid_audit.main_concern_in_original_actions: Fixed >=120 RED, generic slow breathing/fluids as if treatment
first_aid_audit.evidence_backed_principle: AHA decision algorithms prioritize ECG, symptoms, hemodynamic instability and likely cause
first_aid_audit.recommended_action_text: Confirm sensor, pause activity, assess dizziness/chest pain/mental status, request medical review when concerning
first_aid_audit.do_not_automate: Drug treatment, declaring rhythm from pulse alone

GREEN.what_it_means: Resting heart rate is in the normal range.
GREEN.first_aid_action: No action needed. Keep routine monitoring.
GREEN.prevention: Keep the daily aerobic + resistance exercise routine, drink enough fluids, keep a regular sleep schedule and limit excess caffeine.
GREEN.contact_ground_when: Not needed. Report only if symptoms appear (dizziness, palpitations, chest discomfort).

YELLOW_LOW.what_it_means: Heart rate is a little below the normal range (mild). Can be normal in very fit people.
YELLOW_LOW.first_aid_action: Sit or stay secured and rest. Check the sensor, then recheck after 5 minutes. Note any dizziness, tiredness or near-fainting. Avoid hard exercise until it is back in range.
YELLOW_LOW.prevention: Compare against your own baseline trend. Review hydration, sleep and recent training load. Log the value.
YELLOW_LOW.contact_ground_when: If it stays low on repeat checks, keeps trending down, or you feel dizzy or light-headed.

YELLOW_HIGH.what_it_means: Resting heart rate is above the normal range but not critical.
YELLOW_HIGH.first_aid_action: Rest for 5–10 minutes with slow breathing and drink water. Take your temperature (fever raises heart rate). Skip caffeine. Recheck and log the value.
YELLOW_HIGH.prevention: Stay hydrated, manage stress, protect sleep, limit caffeine and keep the exercise routine. Watch the trend over days.
YELLOW_HIGH.contact_ground_when: If it is still high after 15 minutes of rest, keeps rising, comes with fever (possible infection, see DFE-05), or with palpitations.

RED_LOW.first_aid_action: Stop all activity and stay secured and still. Recheck the sensor and measure again. Record an ECG with Tempus Pro if available. Follow the cardiovascular-emergency procedure. Ask a crewmate to stay with you.
RED_LOW.prevention: After recovery: log the event and review training load, medications and hydration with the flight surgeon.

RED_HIGH.first_aid_action: Stop all activity and rest in a secured position with slow breathing. Record an ECG with Tempus Pro and send it. Follow the cardiovascular-emergency procedure. Ask a crewmate to stay with you.
RED_HIGH.prevention: After recovery: log the event; review caffeine, stress, fever, dehydration and medications with the flight surgeon.

RED_SYMPTOM.what_it_means: Heart rate looks normal, but chest pain, fainting or breathlessness is present. Treat as RED.
RED_SYMPTOM.first_aid_action: Stop all activity. Ask a crewmate to stay with you. Record an ECG with Tempus Pro, and follow the cardiovascular-emergency procedure.
RED_SYMPTOM.prevention: After recovery: log the event and review with the flight surgeon before returning to heavy exercise.

vital_signs.why_measured_in_space: Fluid shifts and cardiovascular adaptation; fainting risk at landing
vital_signs.evidence_note: Normal <120 systolic is AHA adult office category, NOT a personalized astronaut target. RED >=180 without organ damage is not automatically a hypertensive emergency. RED low <80 requires individual clinical review.

clinical_evidence_audit.grounded_adult_evidence: 2025 AHA office normal <120; severe >180 plus acute organ injury for hypertensive emergency
clinical_evidence_audit.not_established: No universal astronaut <80 alarm; isolated 180 not always a medical emergency
clinical_evidence_audit.recommendation_for_demo: Pair SBP+DBP, repeat correctly, compare symptoms and individual baseline. Mark critical state provisional.

first_aid_audit.main_concern_in_original_actions: Absolute RED thresholds without end-organ assessment
first_aid_audit.evidence_backed_principle: 2025 AHA classes and emergency criteria differ; measure BP correctly and repeat
first_aid_audit.recommended_action_text: Record paired SBP/DBP and symptoms; escalate serious clinical signs via approved mission protocol
first_aid_audit.do_not_automate: Emergency label based only on >=180 systolic without symptoms/organ findings

GREEN.what_it_means: Systolic blood pressure is in the normal range.
GREEN.first_aid_action: No action needed. Keep routine monitoring.
GREEN.prevention: Keep exercising daily, follow the nutrition and fluid guidance, and use lower-body compression garments and fluid loading before landing as instructed.
GREEN.contact_ground_when: Not needed. Report only if dizziness or fainting appears.

YELLOW_LOW.what_it_means: Systolic pressure is lower than normal (mild).
YELLOW_LOW.first_aid_action: Stay secured and rest. Drink fluids. Move slowly and avoid sudden position changes. Recheck after 5 minutes with the cuff correctly placed. Avoid safety-critical tasks if you feel light-headed.
YELLOW_LOW.prevention: Drink enough fluids, use compression garments as instructed, keep exercising, eat a healthy diet. Follow the pre-landing fluid plan.
YELLOW_LOW.contact_ground_when: If you feel dizzy or faint, or it is still low on recheck.

YELLOW_HIGH.what_it_means: Systolic pressure is above normal but not critical.
YELLOW_HIGH.first_aid_action: Rest quietly for 5 minutes, then recheck with the cuff correctly placed. Avoid caffeine and stress. Log the reading with the time and what you were doing.
YELLOW_HIGH.prevention: Regular exercise, good sleep, stress management and the flight-surgeon nutrition guidance (including salt).
YELLOW_HIGH.contact_ground_when: If readings stay in this range over several days, or any severe headache, chest pain or vision change appears.

RED_LOW.what_it_means: Systolic pressure is critically low. Fainting risk.
RED_LOW.first_aid_action: Stop all activity and stay secured at rest. Drink fluids only if fully alert. Recheck the reading. Ask a crewmate to stay with you and watch for fainting. Follow the cardiovascular procedure.
RED_LOW.prevention: After recovery: review hydration, medications and compression garment use with the flight surgeon.

RED_HIGH.first_aid_action: Stop all activity and rest. Recheck after a few minutes with correct cuff placement. Check for severe headache, chest pain, vision change or weakness. Ask a crewmate to stay with you. Follow the emergency procedure.
RED_HIGH.prevention: After recovery: review salt, stress, caffeine and medications with the flight surgeon.

RED_SYMPTOM.what_it_means: Low blood pressure with dizziness or fainting. Treat as RED even if the number is acceptable.
RED_SYMPTOM.first_aid_action: Stop all activity and stay secured at rest. Ask a crewmate to stay with you. Recheck the reading and follow the cardiovascular procedure.
RED_SYMPTOM.prevention: After recovery: review hydration and compression garment use with the flight surgeon.

vital_signs.evidence_note: Diastolic categories must be read together with systolic. >=120 can be severe, but an emergency requires clinical context/organ injury; <50 not validated as astronaut RED.

clinical_evidence_audit.grounded_adult_evidence: 2025 AHA adult normal <80; evaluate together with systolic and organ-injury signs
clinical_evidence_audit.not_established: No stand-alone astronaut <50 or >=120 emergency cutoff
clinical_evidence_audit.recommendation_for_demo: Use BP as paired measurement; suppress diagnoses from one component alone.

first_aid_audit.main_concern_in_original_actions: Absolute RED thresholds without end-organ assessment
first_aid_audit.evidence_backed_principle: 2025 AHA classes and emergency criteria differ; measure BP correctly and repeat
first_aid_audit.recommended_action_text: Record paired SBP/DBP and symptoms; escalate serious clinical signs via approved mission protocol
first_aid_audit.do_not_automate: Emergency label based only on >=180 systolic without symptoms/organ findings

GREEN.what_it_means: Diastolic blood pressure is in the normal range. Read it together with systolic; the worse of the two decides.
GREEN.first_aid_action: No action needed. Keep routine monitoring.
GREEN.prevention: Keep exercising daily, follow the nutrition and fluid guidance, manage stress and sleep.
GREEN.contact_ground_when: Not needed. Report only if symptoms appear.

YELLOW_LOW.what_it_means: Diastolic pressure is lower than normal (mild).
YELLOW_LOW.first_aid_action: Stay secured and rest. Drink fluids. Move slowly. Recheck after 5 minutes and also check the systolic value.
YELLOW_LOW.prevention: Drink enough fluids, keep exercising, use compression garments as instructed.
YELLOW_LOW.contact_ground_when: If you feel dizzy or faint, or it is still low on recheck.

YELLOW_HIGH.what_it_means: Diastolic pressure is above normal but not critical.
YELLOW_HIGH.first_aid_action: Rest quietly for 5 minutes and recheck with the cuff correctly placed. Avoid caffeine. Log the reading and check systolic too.
YELLOW_HIGH.prevention: Regular exercise, good sleep, stress management and the flight-surgeon nutrition guidance (including salt).
YELLOW_HIGH.contact_ground_when: If readings stay in this range over several days, or any severe headache, chest pain or vision change appears.

RED_LOW.first_aid_action: Stop all activity and stay secured at rest. Recheck both values. Ask a crewmate to stay with you and watch for fainting. Follow the cardiovascular procedure.
RED_LOW.prevention: After recovery: review hydration and medications with the flight surgeon.

RED_HIGH.first_aid_action: Stop all activity and rest. Recheck after a few minutes. Check for severe headache, chest pain, vision change or weakness. Ask a crewmate to stay with you. Follow the emergency procedure.
RED_HIGH.prevention: After recovery: review salt, stress, caffeine and medications with the flight surgeon.

RED_SYMPTOM.what_it_means: High blood pressure with severe headache, chest pain or vision change. Treat as RED.
RED_SYMPTOM.first_aid_action: Stop all activity and rest. Ask a crewmate to stay with you. Recheck both BP values and follow the emergency procedure.
RED_SYMPTOM.prevention: After recovery: log the event and review with the flight surgeon before returning to heavy exercise.

vital_signs.why_measured_in_space: Detects hypoxia from atmosphere or EVA conditions
vital_signs.evidence_note: Adult care oxygen targets are situation-specific (e.g., BTS 94-98%, sometimes 88-92%). FDA cautions oximeter can be inaccurate; check waveform/symptoms/trend. RED <=90 is proposed DEMO flag only.

clinical_evidence_audit.grounded_adult_evidence: BTS targets 94-98% for most acutely ill adults; 88-92% for selected hypercapnia-risk cases
clinical_evidence_audit.not_established: No universal NASA SpO2 cutoff and pulse oximeters have measurement uncertainty
clinical_evidence_audit.recommendation_for_demo: Signal quality + repeated trend + symptoms + mission atmosphere O2/pressure context.

first_aid_audit.main_concern_in_original_actions: Interpreting one value without accuracy warning
first_aid_audit.evidence_backed_principle: FDA/BTS: inspect signal, context and trend; targets vary with physiology
first_aid_audit.recommended_action_text: Verify sensor, repeat, compare with signs and atmosphere/suit oxygen; use approved crew protocol
first_aid_audit.do_not_automate: Titrate oxygen solely from consumer oximeter reading

GREEN.what_it_means: Blood oxygen saturation is in the normal range.
GREEN.first_aid_action: No action needed. Keep routine monitoring.
GREEN.prevention: Keep cabin CO2, pressure and oxygen inside NASA-STD-3001 limits (see Environment_Limits E01–E03). Keep air circulating around sleep and work spots.
GREEN.contact_ground_when: Not needed. Report only if breathlessness or headache appears.

YELLOW_LOW.what_it_means: Oxygen saturation is slightly below normal.
YELLOW_LOW.first_aid_action: Check the sensor first: warm, clean, still finger, good fit. Recheck after 1–2 minutes. Sit upright and breathe slowly and deeply. Check cabin alarms and CO2 (Environment_Limits E01) and make sure air is circulating where you are.
YELLOW_LOW.prevention: Keep ventilation clear, avoid overexertion in poorly ventilated spots, and check the cabin atmosphere regularly.
YELLOW_LOW.contact_ground_when: If it stays below the normal range on repeat checks, or with breathlessness, headache or confusion.

RED_LOW.what_it_means: Oxygen saturation is critically low (hypoxia risk).
RED_LOW.first_aid_action: Quickly recheck the sensor, then stop all activity and sit upright with slow breathing. Check cabin alarms, CO2, pressure and any suit or mask oxygen supply. Follow the hypoxia / emergency procedure. Use supplemental oxygen only as the procedure says. Ask a crewmate to stay with you.
RED_LOW.prevention: After recovery: find and fix the cause (atmosphere, equipment, EVA gear) and log it.

RED_SYMPTOM.what_it_means: Oxygen saturation looks normal, but severe breathlessness, confusion or bluish lips is present. The sensor may be wrong. Treat as RED.
RED_SYMPTOM.first_aid_action: Stop all activity. Ask a crewmate to stay with you. Recheck on another finger, check cabin atmosphere and follow the emergency procedure.
RED_SYMPTOM.prevention: After recovery: log the event and check equipment and cabin atmosphere.

vital_signs.why_measured_in_space: Infection and immune changes; heat stress
vital_signs.evidence_note: Fever >=38 C alone is NOT an automatic medical emergency. NEWS2 scores temperature alongside other variables and mental status. Hypothermia and urgent signs require context.

clinical_evidence_audit.grounded_adult_evidence: NEWS2 recognizes low temperature and fever as parts of a combined assessment
clinical_evidence_audit.not_established: A single fever >=38 is not automatically a RED emergency in a healthy person
clinical_evidence_audit.recommendation_for_demo: Distinguish fever from emergency; use trend, symptoms and associated vitals.

first_aid_audit.main_concern_in_original_actions: 38 C fever automatically equals RED emergency
first_aid_audit.evidence_backed_principle: NEWS2 considers temperature as one factor; severe symptoms are separate
first_aid_audit.recommended_action_text: Recheck temperature and assess infection/heat symptoms along with other vitals
first_aid_audit.do_not_automate: Prescribe antibiotics or call fever alone medical emergency

GREEN.what_it_means: Body temperature is in the normal range.
GREEN.first_aid_action: No action needed. Keep routine monitoring.
GREEN.prevention: Wash hands, clean shared surfaces, keep the cabin within the comfort zone (Environment_Limits E05/E07), sleep well, and report early signs of infection.
GREEN.contact_ground_when: Not needed. Report if fever, chills or new symptoms appear.

YELLOW_LOW.what_it_means: Body temperature is slightly below normal.
YELLOW_LOW.first_aid_action: Re-measure with correct thermometer placement. Add a clothing layer and warm up. Check cabin temperature (Environment_Limits E05). Recheck after 15 minutes.
YELLOW_LOW.prevention: Keep layers available and the cabin in the 20–25 °C comfort zone (Environment_Limits E07).
YELLOW_LOW.contact_ground_when: If it keeps falling, or with shivering, confusion or drowsiness.

YELLOW_HIGH.what_it_means: Body temperature is slightly above normal (low-grade).
YELLOW_HIGH.first_aid_action: Re-measure after 15 minutes of rest (not right after exercise). Drink fluids and remove extra layers. Check cabin temperature and humidity. Watch for chills, cough, sore throat or urinary pain. Check heart rate. Log it.
YELLOW_HIGH.prevention: Hand hygiene, clean shared surfaces, hydration, good sleep. Report early signs of infection (UTI risk: see DFE-05).
YELLOW_HIGH.contact_ground_when: If it reaches fever level, keeps rising, or comes with a rising heart rate.

RED_LOW.first_aid_action: Move to a warmer area and add insulating layers or blankets. Give a warm drink only if fully alert and able to swallow. Recheck with a reliable thermometer. Ask a crewmate to stay with you.
RED_LOW.prevention: After recovery: check cabin and suit thermal controls and log the event.

RED_HIGH.first_aid_action: Confirm with a working thermometer. Rest and drink fluids. Wear light clothing. Use a fever-reducing medicine only as directed by the flight surgeon (check expiry first, see DFE-06). Check heart rate and other vitals, and look for a source (urinary, respiratory, skin). Recheck temperature every few hours and log it.
RED_HIGH.prevention: After recovery: review hand hygiene, surface cleaning and hydration. Report the likely source.
RED_HIGH.contact_ground_when: Contact the flight surgeon now. Fever with a rising heart rate can be an early sign of sepsis (see DFE-05).

RED_SYMPTOM.what_it_means: Temperature looks normal, but severe illness signs (shaking chills, confusion, severe weakness) are present. Treat as RED.
RED_SYMPTOM.first_aid_action: Recheck the thermometer and all other vitals. Rest, drink fluids, and ask a crewmate to stay with you. Follow the emergency procedure.
RED_SYMPTOM.prevention: After recovery: log the event and review with the flight surgeon.

vital_signs.evidence_note: NEWS2 assigns scores to RR <=8 and >=25, but does NOT define universal solo RED emergencies; integrate SpO2, symptoms and consciousness.

clinical_evidence_audit.grounded_adult_evidence: NEWS2 hospital scoring flags <=8 and >=25 at high points but is a combined score
clinical_evidence_audit.not_established: No stand-alone NASA RR RED threshold from NEWS2
clinical_evidence_audit.recommendation_for_demo: Combine with breathing effort, oxygenation and level of consciousness; require clinical escalation policy.

first_aid_audit.main_concern_in_original_actions: Suggesting slow breathing or moving to good airflow generically
first_aid_audit.evidence_backed_principle: NEWS2 + AHA first aid: assess respiratory effort and mental status
first_aid_audit.recommended_action_text: Check effort, responsiveness, SpO2, RR trend and suit/cabin status; crew medical evaluation if concerning
first_aid_audit.do_not_automate: Force breathing rate or change cabin controls without procedure

GREEN.what_it_means: Breathing rate is in the normal range.
GREEN.first_aid_action: No action needed. Keep routine monitoring.
GREEN.prevention: Keep cabin CO2 under the operating limit (Environment_Limits E01), keep air circulating, and keep up regular aerobic exercise.
GREEN.contact_ground_when: Not needed. Report if breathing feels difficult.

YELLOW_LOW.what_it_means: Breathing rate is slightly below normal.
YELLOW_LOW.first_aid_action: Count breaths for a full minute while at rest, without thinking about it. Check for unusual drowsiness. Do not take sedating medicine until you have checked with the flight surgeon. Check cabin CO2 and ventilation.
YELLOW_LOW.prevention: Avoid sedating medications unless prescribed. Keep cabin CO2 low.
YELLOW_LOW.contact_ground_when: If it stays low, or you feel very sleepy or hard to wake.

YELLOW_HIGH.what_it_means: Breathing rate is slightly above normal.
YELLOW_HIGH.first_aid_action: Rest, sit upright and breathe slowly (in for 4 seconds, out for 6). Recheck after 5 minutes. Check cabin CO2 and ventilation alarms. Consider pain, anxiety or fever as causes.
YELLOW_HIGH.prevention: Keep ventilation clear and CO2 low. Keep up aerobic fitness and manage stress.
YELLOW_HIGH.contact_ground_when: If it is still high after rest, or breathing feels hard.

RED_LOW.first_aid_action: Check that you are awake and responsive. Stimulate and wake the person if needed. If they are unresponsive or breathing is very slow, follow the emergency procedure. Check what sedating or opioid medicine was taken, and cabin CO2.
RED_LOW.prevention: After recovery: review medicines and cabin ventilation with the flight surgeon.

RED_HIGH.first_aid_action: Stop all activity and sit upright with slow breathing. Check cabin atmosphere (CO2, pressure, oxygen) and move to an area with good airflow. Follow the respiratory emergency procedure. Ask a crewmate to stay with you.
RED_HIGH.prevention: After recovery: find and fix the cause (atmosphere, fever, anxiety) and log it.

RED_SYMPTOM.what_it_means: Severe breathlessness at any breathing rate. Treat as RED.
RED_SYMPTOM.first_aid_action: Stop all activity and sit upright. Check cabin atmosphere and move to good airflow. Follow the respiratory emergency procedure. Ask a crewmate to stay with you.
RED_SYMPTOM.prevention: After recovery: log the event and check cabin atmosphere and equipment.

vital_signs.why_measured_in_space: Nutrition, stress and metabolic health (named in the challenge brief)
vital_signs.how_measured_in_space: Glucometer (not listed in the provided NASA sources; confirm hardware)
vital_signs.evidence_note: ADA 2026: <70 low, <54 clinically important level 2. Fasting plasma glucose >=126 is a DIAGNOSTIC criterion requiring confirmation, NOT automatic RED emergency. Original >=126 RED is unsupported.

clinical_evidence_audit.grounded_adult_evidence: ADA 2026: <70 low; <54 level-2 hypoglycemia; fasting plasma >=126 diagnostic criterion
clinical_evidence_audit.not_established: >=126 NOT emergency RED; diagnostic confirmation required; capillary device may differ from lab plasma
clinical_evidence_audit.recommendation_for_demo: Flag <70 low; <54 urgent review with symptoms; >=126 diagnostic-review, NOT automatic emergency.
clinical_evidence_audit.flight_use_decision: CHANGE RED HIGH LOGIC BEFORE REAL USE

first_aid_audit.main_concern_in_original_actions: >=126 is diagnostic-range, not acute RED; some oral-sugar instructions need swallowing safeguard
first_aid_audit.evidence_backed_principle: ADA: <70 and <54 are clinically relevant lows; AHA: oral glucose only if alert and can swallow
first_aid_audit.recommended_action_text: For suspected low sugar confirm/recheck; use mission-approved oral glucose guidance only if awake and can swallow; for >=126 refer for diagnostic confirmation
first_aid_audit.do_not_automate: Treat >=126 alone as emergency or give oral intake to unconscious person

GREEN.what_it_means: Fasting blood glucose is in the normal range.
GREEN.first_aid_action: No action needed. Keep routine monitoring.
GREEN.prevention: Eat balanced meals on a regular schedule, log your intake, and keep up daily exercise.
GREEN.contact_ground_when: Not needed. Report only if symptoms appear.

YELLOW_LOW.first_aid_action: If you feel shaky, sweaty or confused, take about 15 g of fast-acting sugar (juice or glucose), then recheck after 15 minutes. After that, eat a proper snack or meal.
YELLOW_LOW.prevention: Do not skip meals. Match food intake to exercise load and log it.
YELLOW_LOW.contact_ground_when: If it stays low, repeats on several days, or symptoms continue.

YELLOW_HIGH.first_aid_action: Confirm you were truly fasting (at least 8 hours without food) and repeat the test another morning. Drink water, avoid sugary food and drinks, and log meals.
YELLOW_HIGH.prevention: Balanced meals, regular exercise, steady weight, limit sugary food and drinks.
YELLOW_HIGH.contact_ground_when: If readings stay in this range for several days, or with thirst, frequent urination or blurred vision.

RED_LOW.first_aid_action: Treat now: take about 15 g of fast-acting sugar (juice or glucose gel) and recheck after 15 minutes; repeat if still low. If confused, unable to swallow safely or unresponsive, give nothing by mouth. Follow the emergency procedure and ask a crewmate for help.
RED_LOW.prevention: After recovery: review meal timing, exercise and any medicines with the flight surgeon.

RED_HIGH.what_it_means: DEMO RED only: fasting glucose >=126 mg/dL is a diagnostic-range result, not an emergency by itself.
RED_HIGH.first_aid_action: Confirm fasting status and measurement; record the value; arrange clinician-directed confirmation and assessment. Use the mission medical protocol if there are acute symptoms.
RED_HIGH.prevention: After review: follow the flight surgeon's advice on diet and exercise.
RED_HIGH.contact_ground_when: Contact flight medical team for interpretation; urgent review if severe symptoms or clinical deterioration.

RED_SYMPTOM.what_it_means: Glucose looks acceptable, but there is confusion or severe weakness. Treat as RED.
RED_SYMPTOM.first_aid_action: Recheck the glucometer and strip. Stay with a crewmate. Follow the emergency procedure.
RED_SYMPTOM.prevention: After recovery: log the event and review with the flight surgeon.

vital_signs.evidence_note: EtCO2 35-45 adult reference; NO verified NASA low-side RED. <30 is a pediatric sedation study definition, NOT NASA guidance. >50 is Miner 2002 ADULT PROCEDURAL SEDATION study criterion (74 patients; abstract), NOT universal astronaut RED; waveform loss and baseline change also mattered.

clinical_evidence_audit.grounded_adult_evidence: Review normal 35-45; Miner 2002 used >50 in ED sedation, plus waveform loss or >10 mmHg change; <30 used in pediatric sedation context
clinical_evidence_audit.not_established: Neither <30 nor >50 is a universal astronaut red limit; no validated numeric lower bound found
clinical_evidence_audit.recommendation_for_demo: Leave numeric low RED blank; treat >50 as study-only candidate; monitor waveform, baseline trend, symptoms and sampling quality.

first_aid_audit.main_concern_in_original_actions: Low and high explanations overclaim and encourage breathing pattern changes
first_aid_audit.evidence_backed_principle: Capnography needs waveform, trends, symptoms and equipment assessment
first_aid_audit.recommended_action_text: Verify waveform and sampling; corroborate RR/SpO2/symptoms; notify trained crew medical person according to mission protocol
first_aid_audit.do_not_automate: Treat <30 or >50 as NASA red, advise arbitrary fan adjustment

GREEN.what_it_means: End-tidal CO2 is in the normal range.
GREEN.first_aid_action: No action needed. Keep routine monitoring.
GREEN.prevention: Keep cabin CO2 under the operating limit (Environment_Limits E01), keep air circulating, and breathe steadily during exercise.
GREEN.contact_ground_when: Not needed. Report if headache or breathlessness appears.

YELLOW_LOW.what_it_means: A low EtCO2 value is nonspecific: sample-line error, ventilation or circulation may affect it.
YELLOW_LOW.first_aid_action: Check signal/waveform quality and sampling connection; repeat measurement; interpret alongside breathing, SpO2, crew symptoms and baseline.
YELLOW_LOW.prevention: Practice calm, steady breathing. Check the sampling line before measuring.
YELLOW_LOW.contact_ground_when: If it stays low with tingling, dizziness or breathlessness.

YELLOW_HIGH.what_it_means: EtCO2 is above the adult reference range; interpretation requires waveform and clinical context.
YELLOW_HIGH.first_aid_action: Recheck capnogram signal and trends; compare breathing rate, SpO2 and cabin CO2; alert the trained medical officer if sustained or symptomatic.
YELLOW_HIGH.prevention: Keep cabin CO2 low and air circulating, especially in sleep areas.
YELLOW_HIGH.contact_ground_when: If it stays high, or with headache, drowsiness or breathlessness.

RED_LOW.what_it_means: No verified numeric low-side RED for an astronaut; this row is reached by a symptom override in the current demo.
RED_LOW.first_aid_action: Assess the crew member and monitor breathing and responsiveness; confirm sensor function; follow mission-approved respiratory emergency checklist.
RED_LOW.prevention: After recovery: log the event and check equipment and cabin atmosphere.

RED_HIGH.what_it_means: The 50 mmHg cutoff came from a small adult procedural-sedation study, not a validated astronaut emergency trigger.
RED_HIGH.first_aid_action: Confirm waveform and repeat reading; evaluate symptoms and other respiratory measurements; use mission-approved medical response if clinically unstable.
RED_HIGH.prevention: After recovery: find and fix the cause of the CO2 build-up and log it.

RED_SYMPTOM.what_it_means: Severe breathlessness or confusion overrides apparently normal EtCO2; headache alone is nonspecific.
RED_SYMPTOM.first_aid_action: Ask for help from trained crew medical personnel; assess clinical status and sensor quality; follow onboard medical emergency procedures.
RED_SYMPTOM.prevention: After recovery: log the event and check cabin atmosphere.

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Systems Operations Support
knowledge_base.condition_name: Communication delay / loss of real-time ground support
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: One-way communication delay
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Delay grows with distance: up to ~20 min one-way cited for Mars (~22.5 min at farthest approach); up to 5 min each way used in HERA simulations
knowledge_base.symptoms: Strain on behavioral health, performance and team coordination
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Handle the situation with onboard procedures, then send a report of what was done and ask for advice (consultation, not real-time guidance); use asynchronous messaging tools
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: After any medical or system event, send a status report even if the reply will be delayed
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Systems Operations Support
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Ability to resolve malfunctions without ground support
knowledge_base.normal_range: LEO and lunar missions under 30 days: ground support can mitigate malfunctions and errors
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Lunar missions over 30 days and any Mars mission: high (red) risk of loss of crew or mission
knowledge_base.symptoms: Crew unable to respond adequately to critical malfunctions or to perform safety-critical procedures
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Use onboard procedures and just-in-time training; rely on pre-mission simulator training (about 300 simulator hours on average for NASA astronauts, per team sheet)
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: When a malfunction cannot be resolved with onboard procedures
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Medical conditions in mission (NASA risk-by-hazard list)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Time to definitive medical care on Earth
knowledge_base.normal_range: ISS: a few hours to about 36 hours
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Moon: about 3 days (possibly 6+); Mars: evacuation timeframe improves only near the end of the mission
knowledge_base.symptoms: Condition worsens before definitive care is available
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Stabilize and sustain the patient with onboard capability for a much longer period; start remote consultation early
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: As soon as a serious injury or illness is suspected
knowledge_base.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Medical conditions in mission (NASA risk-by-hazard list)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: BP, ECG/heart rate, EtCO2, respiration rate, SpO2, temperature, ultrasound
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Tempus Pro with built-in step-by-step guidance (iAssist); telemedicine link; ultrasound learning module
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: See Vital_Thresholds sheet
knowledge_base.symptoms: Depends on the condition
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Use Tempus Pro guidance to collect vitals and images; share data for near-real-time remote diagnosis
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Any RED vital sign, or any YELLOW sign with worsening symptoms
knowledge_base.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Medical conditions in mission (NASA risk-by-hazard list)
knowledge_base.condition_name: Urinary tract infection progressing to sepsis
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Heart rate trend; body temperature
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Rising heart-rate trend and/or fever (38.0 °C or higher)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Fever; worsening condition; rising heart rate
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Act while the problem is small: confirm temperature with a working thermometer, report, and use an effective antibiotic as directed by the flight surgeon
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Fever with a rising heart rate, or any worsening
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Pharm risk (NASA risk-by-hazard list)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Expiry date versus mission end; storage conditions
knowledge_base.normal_range: Within labeled expiry for the whole mission
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Expired or will expire during the mission (team sheet: only ~16% of ISS medications stay within labeled expiry for a Mars round trip)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Reduced or no drug effect
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Check expiry before relying on any medication; report to ground; follow flight-surgeon guidance on alternatives
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Before using any expired or near-expiry medication, especially in an emergency
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Medical conditions in mission (NASA risk-by-hazard list)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Calibration check result
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Calibration fails or the device reports an error
knowledge_base.symptoms: Missing or unreliable readings
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Repeat the measurement; run the calibration check; use a backup device or manual method; report the fault
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If a critical device (vitals monitor, ultrasound) fails during an emergency
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Food acceptability (appeal) and daily intake
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Eating less than needed because of menu fatigue or low morale
knowledge_base.symptoms: Fatigue; nutrient deficiency leading to health problems
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Choose varied, nutritious items; log intake; report repeated low intake
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If low intake continues for several days, or fatigue or weight loss appear
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Bone mineral density change from pre-flight baseline
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Average loss of about 1–1.5% per month in space (team sheet; verify)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Bone weakness; increased fracture risk; premature osteoporosis
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Do your resistance exercise routine; keep scheduled bone scans; follow flight-surgeon advice on diet and medication
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If a scan shows loss beyond plan, or after any impact with bone pain
knowledge_base.action_focus: Prevention: do the routine measures that stop the problem

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Vision changes; optic disc swelling, retinal folds, globe flattening (imaging)
knowledge_base.normal_range: No new vision change; stable imaging
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Any new or worsening blurred vision or near-vision change; abnormal imaging
knowledge_base.symptoms: Optic nerve swelling; retinal folds; flattening of the back of the eye; vision problems
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Record any vision change; do eye checks as scheduled; report findings (B-vitamin and thigh-cuff studies are research, not instructions)
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Any new or worsening vision change
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
knowledge_base.condition_name: Muscle weakness and reduced physical fitness
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Muscle strength, aerobic fitness, endurance versus pre-mission
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Exercise equipment performance logs; periodic fitness self-evaluation
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: More than 20% loss of pre-mission fitness (team sheet)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Weakness; reduced endurance; poorer coordination; higher risk of falls and injury
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Do daily resistance and aerobic exercise; complete periodic fitness self-evaluations
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If loss exceeds 20% or you have an injury or fall
knowledge_base.action_focus: Prevention: do the routine measures that stop the problem

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Blood pressure (sitting and standing); heart rate
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Blood pressure cuff or Tempus Pro
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Low BP with dizziness; higher fainting risk at landing
knowledge_base.symptoms: Light-headedness; fainting
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Use lower-body compression garments; drink fluids before landing; keep exercising; eat a healthy diet
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Fainting, or low BP with symptoms
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Heart rate; heart rhythm (ECG)
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Irregular rhythm, or heart rate outside Vital_Thresholds
knowledge_base.symptoms: Palpitations, dizziness, chest discomfort or breathlessness (general clinical signs)
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Record an ECG, rest, and follow the cardiovascular-emergency procedure and training
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Any irregular rhythm with symptoms, immediately
knowledge_base.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Venous Haemostasis study (HRP research)
knowledge_base.condition_name: Venous blood clot (internal jugular vein thrombosis)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Jugular vein ultrasound flow; blood pressure; blood tests
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Ultrasound guided in real time; images read by Earth radiologists
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Stagnant or retrograde flow (team sheet: 6 of 11 crew by about flight day 50; 1 clot; verify)
knowledge_base.symptoms: May be silent: the crew member with a clot had no headache or flushed face
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Do the guided ultrasound and send images to ground; follow-up ultrasound confirms; treatment is decided by the flight surgeon (lower-body negative pressure improved flow in 10 of 17 sessions, per team sheet)
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Any abnormal flow finding or suspected clot
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor and Vestibular Function
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Balance, head-eye and hand-eye coordination, orientation
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Self-report; simple balance and coordination tests
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Dizziness, nausea, balance or coordination problems
knowledge_base.symptoms: Motion sickness; light-headedness; difficulty walking or operating a vehicle
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Move slowly; avoid vehicle operation and safety-critical tasks until recovered; log symptoms
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If symptoms persist or prevent safety-critical tasks
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Renal stone risk (NASA risk interface analysis)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Hydration status; urinary calcium; abdominal pain
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Fluid-intake log; urine samples; ultrasound for a suspected stone
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Low urine volume or high urinary calcium; severe lower abdominal pain; blood in urine
knowledge_base.symptoms: Dehydration; increased calcium excretion from bone
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Prevention: hydrate and follow nutrition guidance. Suspected stone: ultrasound, pain medication, rest, report and ask for advice
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Severe abdominal or flank pain, or blood in urine
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Injury from Dynamic Loads
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Forces during landing; crew discomfort surveys with spacecraft sensor data
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Injury during landing
knowledge_base.symptoms: Pain or injury after landing
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Follow landing and restraint procedures; report any pain after landing
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Any post-landing injury or pain
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Sleep duration
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Wrist actigraphy (motion, sleep, light); sleep log
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Less than 7 hours for 2 consecutive nights
knowledge_base.symptoms: Fatigue; reduced alertness; poor concentration
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Protect your sleep window, reduce nonessential workload, and check cabin noise and lighting (see HCE rows)
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If the warning persists after you adjusted schedule and environment, or sleepiness affects safety-critical tasks
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Sleep/wake timing variation versus personal baseline
knowledge_base.normal_range: Consistent sleep and wake times relative to personal baseline
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Significant deviation from baseline for 2 or more days
knowledge_base.symptoms: Daytime sleepiness; fatigue; difficulty staying alert
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Keep a consistent sleep-wake schedule; review lighting and work schedule
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If deviation continues despite schedule changes
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Sleep efficiency
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Less than 85% repeatedly
knowledge_base.symptoms: Unrefreshing sleep; frequent awakenings; daytime fatigue
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Review your sleep environment and keep monitoring
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If low efficiency continues alongside daytime fatigue
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Self-reported stress score
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: In-app questionnaire (team design); HRP Standard Measures include psychological measures
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Score 4–5, or a rise of 2 points from baseline
knowledge_base.symptoms: Feeling overwhelmed; irritability; difficulty relaxing
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Use stress-management strategies and review your workload; ask for support
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If high scores persist or affect your work or sleep
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Self-reported mood score
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Score 2 or lower, or a persistent decrease from baseline
knowledge_base.symptoms: Low motivation; reduced interest; negative mood
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Connect with crewmates, use scheduled psychological support, and keep tracking your mood
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If low mood persists. Any thought of self-harm: tell a crewmate and ground medical or psychological support immediately
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Self-reported mental fatigue score
knowledge_base.normal_range: Low and stable relative to personal baseline
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Score 4–5 on 2 consecutive assessments
knowledge_base.symptoms: Difficulty concentrating; mental exhaustion; reduced alertness
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Take recovery time, review workload, and reassess
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If fatigue persists or affects safety-critical tasks
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Attention test score
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: More than 10% decrease from baseline on repeated tests
knowledge_base.symptoms: Reduced focus; more errors; difficulty completing tasks
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Repeat the test; review sleep and fatigue; adjust workload
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If the decrease repeats across tests
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Reaction time
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: More than 20% increase from baseline on repeated tests
knowledge_base.symptoms: Slower responses; reduced alertness; delayed reactions
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Repeat the test; review sleep and fatigue; keep monitoring
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If slowing repeats, especially before safety-critical tasks
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Memory test score
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: More than 10% decrease from baseline on repeated tests
knowledge_base.symptoms: Difficulty recalling information; memory errors
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Repeat the test; review sleep patterns; keep monitoring
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If the decrease repeats across tests
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Inadequate Teamwork
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Self-reported team cohesion or conflict rating
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Sustained drop, or an unresolved conflict
knowledge_base.symptoms: Tension; miscommunication; withdrawal
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Use structured crew debriefs; address issues early and calmly; ask for support
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If conflict is unresolved or affects safety or work
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Severe or persistent change in mood, behavior or stress; any self-harm thoughts
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Any severe change, or any self-harm thought
knowledge_base.symptoms: Marked withdrawal, hopelessness, agitation, inability to function
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Stay with a crewmate and contact ground medical or psychological support immediately
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Immediately
knowledge_base.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6004 (CO2 limit)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: CO2 partial pressure (ppCO2), 1-hour average
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: 1-hour mean above 3 mmHg (an operating limit, not a poisoning dose)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Headache; tiredness; trouble focusing; sometimes poor sleep or nausea
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Check the reading and CO2 removal and air circulation; alert the crew; follow the cabin-atmosphere checklist
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If symptoms persist after the reading returns to range, or the cause cannot be found
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Hypoxia; NASA-STD-3001 V2 6003 (PIO2 range)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Inspired oxygen partial pressure (PIO2) with cabin pressure; SpO2
knowledge_base.normal_range: Within the mission-approved PIO2 range (for reference, sea-level normoxic PIO2 is about 139–168 mmHg)
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Outside the approved range for that mission and exposure time
knowledge_base.symptoms: Dizziness; headache; shortness of breath; confusion if severe
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Verify O2 and pressure sensors, notify the crew, check SpO2, and use the mission oxygen/pressure procedure
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Immediately if confusion, severe breathlessness or a low SpO2 appears
knowledge_base.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6002 (inert diluent gas)
knowledge_base.condition_name: Too much oxygen / wrong gas mixture
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: O2 partial pressure and inert diluent percentage
knowledge_base.normal_range: At least 30% diluent gas in the nominal mixture
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Diluent below 30%, or PIO2 outside the mission limit
knowledge_base.symptoms: May be symptom-free at first; prolonged high O2 exposure can affect the lungs
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Flag the abnormal mix; review atmosphere controls and fire-safety procedure; do not change the gas mixture except by approved procedure
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Any abnormal mixture reading
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6006 (total pressure range)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Total pressure and pressure trend
knowledge_base.normal_range: Above 34.5 and up to 103 kPa for indefinite exposure; the target setpoint may be narrower
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: At or below 34.5 kPa or above 103 kPa; any unexpected pressure loss
knowledge_base.symptoms: Ear discomfort; difficulty breathing; light-headedness
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Raise a pressure alert; check for leaks; follow the vehicle pressure checklist
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Immediately for any unexplained pressure loss
knowledge_base.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6007 (rate of pressure change)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Pressure change over time
knowledge_base.normal_range: Controlled changes above 1 psi: no faster than 13.5 psi/min
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Faster than the approved rate, or any unplanned drop needing investigation
knowledge_base.symptoms: Ear or sinus pain; breathing problems; severe cases are emergencies
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Notify the crew immediately and open the emergency depressurization guidance
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Immediately
knowledge_base.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6012 and 6013 (temperature and humidity)
knowledge_base.condition_name: Cabin too hot or too cold
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Temperature with relative humidity
knowledge_base.normal_range: Inside NASA's combined envelope: operating limit 18 °C/75% RH to 27 °C/25% RH; crew performance zone 20–25 °C and 30–60% RH
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Measured pair falls outside the envelope
knowledge_base.symptoms: Discomfort; fatigue; sweating or chills; heat stress if severe
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Read both values together; check the environmental control system and crew comfort
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If heat or cold stress symptoms appear, or the system cannot be corrected
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6012 (temperature and humidity)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Relative humidity, cabin temperature, moisture reports
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Outside the envelope, or recurring condensation needing inspection
knowledge_base.symptoms: Dry eyes or throat; damp surfaces; possible mold growth over time
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Check humidity controls and wet surfaces; log a maintenance check
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If condensation or mold signs recur
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6107 (ventilation)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Airflow by location with local CO2
knowledge_base.normal_range: Enough air mixing to avoid stagnant areas near the crew
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Low airflow with local CO2 or heat buildup (set point depends on habitat layout)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Stuffiness; headache; overheating
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Compare nearby sensors; inspect fans and vents using the approved procedure
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If headache or stuffiness persists after airflow checks
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6052 (particulate matter)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Total suspended dust and respirable dust (< 2.5 µm)
knowledge_base.normal_range: Total dust < 3 mg/m³; respirable fraction < 1 mg/m³
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Either limit reached or exceeded (values are for ordinary, nonreactive dust)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Eye and airway irritation; coughing
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Check filtration and the likely dust source; follow the particle-cleanup procedure
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If respiratory symptoms continue
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6053 (lunar dust)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Lunar dust particles < 10 µm, time-weighted concentration
knowledge_base.normal_range: < 0.3 mg/m³ for the NASA-specified intermittent exposure scenario
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: 0.3 mg/m³ or more in that scenario (not a general rule for Mars dust)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Eye or throat irritation; breathing discomfort
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Use habitat dust-control and post-EVA cleaning steps; record exposure
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If breathing discomfort develops after EVA
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6050 (atmosphere contamination limit)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Concentration of the identified gas and exposure duration
knowledge_base.normal_range: Below that substance's NASA SMAC value for the exposure period
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Exceeds the SMAC for that exact chemical and duration (no universal VOC number)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Irritation; headache; dizziness or nausea depending on the chemical
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Identify the suspected contaminant; alert the crew; follow the toxic-exposure checklist

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6024 (combustion monitoring)
knowledge_base.condition_name: Smoke or harmful gases after a fire
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Fire/smoke detector; CO and other combustion gas readings
knowledge_base.normal_range: No active smoke or fire; combustion gases inside mission limits
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Any smoke or fire alarm, or a gas-specific limit exceeded
knowledge_base.symptoms: Coughing; eye irritation; headache; confusion if exposure is serious
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Start the fire / toxic-atmosphere emergency procedure and decide with the crew whether to leave the affected area
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Immediately
knowledge_base.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6026 and 6051 (potable water)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Water chemistry and microbial tests; conductivity/TOC where fitted
knowledge_base.normal_range: Meets spacecraft water-quality requirements and microbial tests
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Failed required test, harmful organism detected, or a chemical limit passed
knowledge_base.symptoms: Stomach upset or infection (often no immediate symptoms)
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Mark the source as suspect; follow sampling, isolation and water-safety steps
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: On any failed test or unexplained stomach illness in the crew
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 6059 (microbial air contamination)
knowledge_base.condition_name: Microbes building up in the habitat
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Air and surface samples (CFU or lab identification)
knowledge_base.normal_range: Within mission microbial limits; no medically significant pathogens
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: A relevant organism found, or an approved sample limit exceeded
knowledge_base.symptoms: Allergy-like symptoms; rash; infection (not always visible)
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Request a confirmation sample; check the cleaning process; inform the medical team
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: When a pathogen is found or several crew have symptoms
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 (acoustics)
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Noise spectrum compared against NC curves
knowledge_base.normal_range: Typical long-mission target: work ≤ NC-50; sleep ≤ NC-40
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Spectrum exceeds the relevant NC curve (NC is not dBA)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Poor sleep; fatigue; difficulty hearing instructions
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Identify the noisy area or equipment; propose approved maintenance or a quieter sleep setup
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If noise keeps disturbing sleep or communication
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 8055 (lighting)
knowledge_base.condition_name: Not enough useful light during the day
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Melanopic EDI at eye level; DER
knowledge_base.normal_range: During scheduled daytime: EDI ≥ 250 lux; DER ≥ 0.7
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Daytime EDI < 250 lux or DER < 0.7
knowledge_base.symptoms: Sleep–wake timing can shift; less alertness
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Check the lighting schedule and spectrum; adjust to approved daytime lighting
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If sleep timing or alertness is affected
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: NASA-STD-3001 V2 8055 (lighting)
knowledge_base.condition_name: Too much stimulating light before sleep
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Melanopic EDI and DER before bedtime
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: In the pre-sleep period: EDI outside 6–10 lux or DER > 0.3
knowledge_base.symptoms: Trouble falling asleep; poorer sleep
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Switch to approved dim, blue-reduced lighting in the pre-sleep period
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: If sleep problems continue
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care and monitoring: log it and report if it persists

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Symptoms with periodic blood, saliva or microbiology tests
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Blood and saliva samples (HRP Immune Biomarkers); symptom log
knowledge_base.normal_range: Compared with your own medical baseline; no single continuous-sensor number
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Clinically important change as set by the flight medical team (not a wearable-only diagnosis)
knowledge_base.symptoms: Rash; infection symptoms; possible latent-virus reactivation
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Log your observations and report to the medical staff
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Any rash, fever or infection signs
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Decompression Sickness; NASA-STD-3001 V2 6008
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Joint pain; breathing difficulty; neurological signs after pressure change
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Crew symptom report; EVA protocol compliance
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Pain, breathing effects, or stroke-like symptoms after a pressure change
knowledge_base.symptoms: Pain; in severe cases breathing effects or blocked blood vessels with stroke-like symptoms
knowledge_base.recommended_action: End the spacewalk safely but rapidly and return to the pressurized spacecraft; do the pure-oxygen prebreathe before spacewalks
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Immediately
knowledge_base.action_focus: Emergency action now and contact the flight surgeon

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Injury and Compromised Performance from EVA
knowledge_base.condition_name: Injury and compromised performance from spacewalks
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Cognitive fatigue; injury; suit CO2 and O2 conditions
knowledge_base.normal_range: No pain or unusual fatigue; suit conditions normal
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Pain, unusual fatigue or slowed thinking during or after EVA
knowledge_base.symptoms: Cognitive fatigue; injury
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Follow EVA prebreathe and timeline; stop and report pain, fatigue or slowed thinking; keep up exercise for bone and muscle
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: Immediately for pain, confusion or abnormal suit readings
knowledge_base.action_focus: Self-care first aid now, and report to ground the same day

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Radiation-Induced Cancers
knowledge_base.metric_to_monitor: Individual cumulative dose and exposure-induced death risk (REID)
knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Personal and area dosimeters; flight-surgeon dose tracking
knowledge_base.normal_range: Tracked per individual; ALARA principle (as low as reasonably achievable)
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: NASA policy: career cancer-death risk up to 3% REID, with 95% confidence (limit depends on age and sex). A 2021 National Academies report recommended a 600 mSv career limit (verify the current NASA value)
knowledge_base.symptoms: No immediate symptoms; long-term cancer risk
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Review your cumulative dose with the flight surgeon; follow ALARA practices and shelter guidance
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: When a dosimeter alarm sounds or the plan's dose budget is approached
knowledge_base.action_focus: Prevention: do the routine measures that stop the problem

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Radiation-Induced Cancers

knowledge_base.measured_in_space: Active neutron spectrometer (CANS, under development); bubble detectors used previously on ISS
knowledge_base.normal_range: Monitored continuously; neutrons contribute about 30% of total radiation on the ISS
knowledge_base.warning_threshold: Readings above the mission plan (limits set by the flight surgeon)
knowledge_base.symptoms: No immediate symptoms; biological damage risk
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Move to protected areas as directed; keep exposure as low as reasonably achievable
knowledge_base.contact_ground_when: When readings rise above plan
knowledge_base.action_focus: Prevention: do the routine measures that stop the problem

knowledge_base.related_nasa_risk_or_standard: Risk of Radiation-Induced Cancers

knowledge_base.symptoms: Dose can be very high for unprotected crew (exceptional events: 1–3 Sv unprotected, per a secondary source)

knowledge_base.symptoms: No immediate symptoms
knowledge_base.recommended_action: Follow ALARA and the medical follow-up plan; research on countermeasures is ongoing

etco2_review.question: Is 35-45 mmHg a reference?
etco2_review.finding: Yes, normal adult ETCO2 is commonly 35-45 mmHg
etco2_review.meaning_for_astra: A useful reference range, not a mission emergency zone

etco2_review.question: Can we use <30 mmHg as astronaut RED?
etco2_review.finding: No. <30 appears in a 2025 PEDIATRIC procedural sedation study as a respiratory-event definition
etco2_review.meaning_for_astra: Do not adopt it as universal flight red. Correct to leave Critical_Low blank.

etco2_review.question: Can we use >50 mmHg as astronaut RED?
etco2_review.finding: No. Miner et al 2002: 74 adults undergoing procedural sedation in an emergency department
etco2_review.meaning_for_astra: 50 was a STUDY respiratory-depression criterion, not a general NASA limit

etco2_review.question: Was the 2002 full paper reviewed?
etco2_review.finding: Abstract reviewed; independent ACEP clinical policy also summarizes this study
etco2_review.meaning_for_astra: Do not claim direct full-text review of the original 2002 paper

etco2_review.question: What else did the 2002 study use?
etco2_review.finding: Absent capnogram waveform and >10 mmHg change from baseline appeared in post-hoc detection
etco2_review.meaning_for_astra: Waveform presence and change often more informative than one number

etco2_review.question: What can low EtCO2 mean?
etco2_review.finding: Ventilation, pulmonary perfusion, metabolism or measurement/sampling issue
etco2_review.meaning_for_astra: Check signal quality; never label low EtCO2 automatically as disease

etco2_review.question: Is cabin CO2 the same as EtCO2?
etco2_review.finding: No. Cabin ppCO2 measures environmental exposure; ETCO2 measures exhaled gas concentration at end expiration
etco2_review.meaning_for_astra: Keep environmental sensor and physiological capnograph as separate measurements

etco2_review.question: Does NASA publish a general EtCO2 RED for all astronauts here?
etco2_review.finding: No universal astronaut alarm threshold was established by the NASA resources consulted
etco2_review.meaning_for_astra: Keep source confidence C, mark as requiring crew-medical signoff

etco2_review.question: Safer prototype behavior
etco2_review.finding: Validate waveform -> check trend -> assess symptoms/RR/SpO2 -> request crew-medical assessment
etco2_review.meaning_for_astra: Show Investigation Needed, not automated diagnosis or treatment from ETCO2 alone
